method: The unit is the collective FOMC funds-rate decision statement as published on the release date. Each record links to the Board and identifies the wording used. Individual dissents, press conferences, minutes, portfolio policy and subsequent outcomes are excluded from the wording score.

The ordinal score measures prospective policy-rate inclination. Positive values signal tightening and negative values signal accommodation. An explicit low-for-long commitment can score −2 even when the rate stays unchanged. A conditional future cut scores −1. Only explicit patience about undirected rate changes qualifies for 0 in this sample. Broad economic support or a commitment to price stability alone leaves the rate score unavailable.

The first applicable wording rule wins. For example, the December 2014 statement introduced eventual normalization while explicitly recalling its earlier low-rate pledge. The new policy wording takes precedence. Different horizons, conditionality within a category and dissent can matter even when two scores coincide.

The shift subtracts the immediately preceding funds-rate statement's score from the current score. Both must be available. The scale is ordinal. A two-step shift is a change of rubric categories and has no basis-point or probability interpretation.
Short extracts preserve the source wording with normalized whitespace, apostrophes and dashes. An ellipsis marks an omission. A release time appears when the statement explicitly prints Eastern time.

The action is the change in the announced federal funds point target or the upper bound of a target range, in basis points. A hold is zero. The February 2000 change is stated in the release. The December 2008 switch from a point to a range has no comparable single change.

Risk tags reproduce a separate, limited set of majority risk-balance and emphasis formulations. An untagged statement can still discuss macroeconomic risks. The price-stability emphasis tag records explicit emphasis only. Target actions, risk tags and market prices never enter the wording rules.

The rubric was developed retrospectively. Scores use only the dated statement, but the rules themselves were not available historically. They are descriptive, and have no claimed out-of-sample accuracy or predictive interpretation.

coverage.scope: Scheduled and intermeeting funds-rate decision statements. Operational, liquidity-only and balance-sheet-only releases are outside this series.

patient-normalization.label: Patience before normalization
patient-normalization.rationale: The Committee named withdrawal of accommodation and said it could wait before starting.

cut-hurdle.label: Condition for a future cut
cut-hurdle.rationale: A reduction was the specific adjustment under discussion. The Committee set a disinflation hurdle before it could proceed.

liftoff-hurdle.label: Conditions for a future increase
liftoff-hurdle.rationale: The Committee identified a rate increase and conditioned it on further progress in the economy.

additional-firming.label: Additional firming under consideration
additional-firming.rationale: The Committee singled out possible additional tightening and left the need for it conditional.

upcoming-increase.label: Increase expected soon
upcoming-increase.rationale: The statement explicitly anticipated near-term liftoff.

ongoing-increases.label: Ongoing rate increases
ongoing-increases.rationale: The Committee expected a sequence of rate increases.

measured-tightening.label: Measured removal of accommodation
measured-tightening.rationale: The Committee envisaged removing accommodation at a measured pace.

gradual-increases.label: Gradual rate increases expected
gradual-increases.rationale: The Committee explicitly described a path of gradual increases in the policy rate.

low-rate-threshold.label: Low rates until specified conditions
low-rate-threshold.rationale: The Committee expected the exceptionally low target range to persist until an economic condition was met.

low-rate-horizon.label: Low rates for an extended horizon
low-rate-horizon.rationale: The Committee explicitly envisaged a sustained period of accommodation or exceptionally low policy rates.

patient-two-sided.label: Wait before deciding on adjustments
patient-two-sided.rationale: The Committee explicitly signalled patience about future adjustments without singling out increases or cuts.

support-economy.label: Economic support, instrument open
support-economy.rationale: The Committee pledged to respond to economic conditions while leaving its next policy-rate adjustment open.

current-stance.label: Current stance judged appropriate
current-stance.rationale: The Committee endorsed its current setting without specifying how long it expected to maintain the policy rate.

open-path.label: Path left open
open-path.rationale: The majority described future assessment or flexibility and specified no rate direction or holding horizon.

unspecified.label: No explicit rate outlook
unspecified.rationale: No prospective rate direction, holding horizon or explicit wait signal was identified in the majority's statement.
